data.narrative:
BurnBot is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Anukool Lakhina and Waleed 'Lee' Haddad that has raised $25M to date. The relevant comp universe spans 9 private frontier-tech peers in climate and energy alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA), though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage clustering to support a robust peer-median approach.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation lens. Using total capital raised ($25M) as a proxy for pre-money value, a standard Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $50M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-filter datapoints; the broader climate and energy comp set of 9 private companies and 1 public name does not cluster tightly enough around BurnBot's stage and valuation tier to generate reliable cross-sectional support.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M (low) to $57M (high), with a median of $50M. This estimate rests entirely on stage-progression mechanics and carries material uncertainty around the appropriate step-up multiplier and the absence of direct peer-valuation anchoring. Key risks to this range include execution on product roadmap, capital efficiency relative to sector norms, and macro conditions affecting frontier-tech funding.
